minutes.headline: COA votes to request a second-floor elevator/lift feasibility study for the FY27 town capital plan
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging heard updates on the Nashoba Valley Hospital site and regional ambulance shortages, fire department staffing, and the Marshall Park renovation ballot question, then approved its minutes with a wording change about on-call firefighters. It voted to ask the town's facilities department to add an accessibility study for the Eagle House's second floor to the FY27 capital plan, reviewed FY26 budget changes and proposed FY27 staffing requests (a meal-site buffer, a program coordinator, and an upgraded outreach/assistant-director role), and closed with a director's report covering the kitchen renovation, spring programming, and a longtime employee's retirement.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging voted to ask the town's facilities department to add a feasibility study for elevator or lift access to the Eagle House's second floor to the FY27 capital plan.
The director laid out FY27 staffing requests: a meal-site funding buffer, a new program coordinator position, and an upgraded assistant-director/outreach title with a raise.
FY26 budget review showed the COA losing a part-time outreach assistant position while adding two kitchen aide positions and a full-time meal site manager.
The board amended its prior minutes to describe fire department coverage as "on-call firefighters" rather than volunteers before the minutes go to town hall.
The board set aside a proposed senior healthcare advocacy team, agreeing to return with concrete ideas at the next meeting rather than act now.

why_it_matters: A capital-plan request for an elevator or lift study is an early step that would need to survive the town's FY27 capital budgeting process before any accessibility work at the senior center happens.
The FY27 staffing and program requests -- a program coordinator, a retitled assistant-director role with a raise, and meal-program funding -- would draw on the town budget residents vote on.
The FY26 staffing changes show how the meal program and outreach work are currently being covered, which bears on how the FY27 requests are judged.
